item.text:
**5B.3 Research Note**

Overall, the 2024 record is more positive than negative on macro stability and monetary credibility, but mixed on fiscal discipline and long-term investment conditions. Jokowi left Indonesia with inflation and the rupiah broadly contained, a deficit still inside the legal ceiling, and repeated institutional emphasis on prudence. The main negatives are higher election-year spending, a cancelled planned tax hike after year-end, and weak execution/foreign investment in Nusantara.

**Accepted claims**

- **Indonesia Economy Projected to Remain Resilient** — World Bank, 2024-06-24, https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/24/indonesia-economy-projected-to-remain-resilient  
  The World Bank said Indonesia’s robust macroeconomic policy framework helped attract investment, and stressed prudent, credible, transparent macro policy plus fiscal space for social protection and human capital. This is strong positive evidence for macro stability and investment conditions.  
  IDs: `5B.3`, also `5B.1`

- **IMF Staff Completes 2024 Article IV Mission to Indonesia** — IMF, 2024-06-14, https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/06/14/pr24221-imf-staff-completes-2024-article-iv-mission-to-indonesia  
  IMF staff said Indonesia’s outlook remained positive, inflation would stay in target, policy should remain prudent, and the fiscal rule and credibility should be preserved. This is strong evidence for fiscal responsibility and monetary credibility.  
  IDs: `5B.3`

- **Monetary Policy Report - Quarter I 2024** — Bank Indonesia, 2024-04-30, https://www.bi.go.id/en/publikasi/laporan/Pages/Laporan-Kebijakan-Moneter-Triwulan-I-2024.aspx  
  Bank Indonesia raised rates preemptively to defend rupiah stability and keep inflation inside the 2.5% ±1% corridor, while using pro-market instruments to attract inflows. This supports a positive finding on monetary credibility and investment conditions.  
  IDs: `5B.3`

- **Bank Indonesia Institutional Report 2024** — Bank Indonesia, published 2025, covering 2024, https://www.bi.go.id/en/publikasi/laporan/Pages/LKBI-2024.aspx  
  BI said 2024 growth reached 5.03%, inflation stayed at 1.57% in December 2024, the rupiah remained under control, reserves were buoyant, and policy coordination with government strengthened. This is strong evidence of macro stability and credible monetary management.  
  IDs: `5B.3`

- **Indonesia books lower-than-expected 2024 fiscal deficit** — Reuters via Investing.com, 2025-01-05, https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/indonesias-budget-deficit-in-2024-at-23-of-gdp-3796361  
  Reuters reported that Indonesia’s 2024 budget deficit was 2.29% of GDP, below the 3% legal ceiling and below the earlier 2.7% estimate. This is strong positive evidence for fiscal responsibility, though the deficit widened from 2023.  
  IDs: `5B.3`

- **Indonesia launches 'Golden Visa' to lure foreign investors, boost economy** — Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-07-25, https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/indonesia-launches-golden-visa-to-lure-foreign-investors-boost-economy-3535351  
  Jokowi launched a long-term visa scheme explicitly to attract foreign investors and boost the economy. This supports a positive reading on long-term investment conditions.  
  IDs: `5B.3`, also `5B.1`

- **Indonesia hails Chinese firm as first foreign investor in troubled new capital** — Reuters via ThePrint, 2024-09-25, https://theprint.in/world/indonesia-hails-chinese-firm-as-first-foreign-investor-in-troubled-new-capital/2283073/  
  Jokowi touted the first foreign investment in Nusantara, but the report also said the project had faced delays and weak foreign interest. This is mixed evidence: investment promotion was real, but conditions were not fully healthy.  
  IDs: `5B.3`

- **Analysis: A decade of Jokowi, Indonesia’s democracy icon, leaves illiberal legacy, critics say** — Reuters via ThePrint, 2024-10-14, https://theprint.in/world/analysis-a-decade-of-jokowi-indonesias-democracy-icon-leaves-illiberal-legacy-critics-say/2310394/  
  Reuters said Jokowi left strong growth and infrastructure, but also patronage and dynastic politics. For this lens, the economic-relevant part is that growth/infrastructure outcomes were real, but broader governance quality was weaker than ideal for long-term investment certainty.  
  IDs: `5B.3`, also `5B.1`

**Negative or cautionary evidence**

- **Indonesia says 2024 budget deficit lower than 2.7% of GDP estimate** — Reuters via Investing.com, 2025-01-01, https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/indonesia-says-2024-budget-deficit-lower-than-27-of-gdp-estimate-3793456  
  Reuters said spending rose more than 6% in 2024 due to election costs, Nusantara construction, and welfare programs. That is cautionary evidence that fiscal policy was being stretched by political and flagship-project commitments, even if still within rule bounds.  
  IDs: `5B.3`

- **Indonesia books lower-than-expected 2024 fiscal deficit** — Reuters via Investing.com, 2025-01-05, https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/indonesias-budget-deficit-in-2024-at-23-of-gdp-3796361  
  Reuters noted that authorities cancelled a planned tax hike after year-end, which suggests policy flexibility but also some fragility in revenue strategy. This weakens, but does not overturn, the fiscal-responsibility picture.  
  IDs: `5B.3`

- **Indonesia’s foreign investment in 2024** — Reuters via Reuters Connect / NurPhoto, 2024-08-14, https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/investment-landscape-in-indonesia/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjQ6bmV3c21sX01UMU5VUlBITzAwMFdSMzhEQw  
  The Reuters caption reported that direct investment in the first half of 2024 was growing strongly, which is positive, but it is only a caption-level market signal rather than a detailed policy assessment. I include it because it supports the investment-conditions side, but it is weaker evidence than the World Bank or IMF.  
  IDs: `5B.3`

**Synthesis**
- Best positive case: Jokowi preserved macro stability, kept inflation and the rupiah under control, and ended 2024 with a deficit still below the legal 3% cap.
- Best negative case: election-year spending rose, a tax hike was later cancelled, and the flagship capital project still struggled to attract foreign investment.
- Net: **mostly positive on macro stability and monetary credibility; mixed on fiscal discipline and long-term investment conditions**.

**Search gap**
- I did not find strong direct evidence that Jokowi lost monetary credibility in 2024 or that Bank Indonesia was overtly politicized.
- I also did not find a clean, direct 2024 source showing major fiscal profligacy beyond the election/Nusantara spending pressures and the later cancelled tax hike.
